summary: HTML loader fetches and executes remote code from a mutable Cloudflare Worker URL
details: The package ships a single index.html whose only behavior is to fetch https://loader.p2pgames.workers.dev/ with a custom `x-access: p2p` header and inject the response into the DOM via document.open()/document.write()/document.close(). Whatever JavaScript the worker returns at request time runs in the consumer's browser context. There is no subresource integrity check, no version pinning, and no signature verification; the worker operator can change the served payload at any time without any change to the package. There are no npm lifecycle scripts, so `npm install` itself does not execute remote code — the harm fires when a developer or end-user actually loads the HTML file as advertised. Routing to human review: the loader pattern is structurally a remote-code-execution channel (mutable URL, attacker-controlled bytes, no verification), but it does not auto-execute on install/require and the destination is a generic Cloudflare Workers subdomain whose operator identity has not been verified against a publisher.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
